title: Abuse is one of the hardest questions to bring before God… because it feels like silence where there should have been thunder.
paragraphs: Abuse is one of the hardest questions to bring before God… because it feels like silence where there should have been thunder.
Why didn’t He stop it?
Why didn’t He step in?
Why does a holy God allow something so unholy?
Let’s not soften it.

Abuse is evil.
Not “a lesson.”
Not “a misunderstanding.”
Evil.
And Scripture never pretends otherwise.
God does not approve of abuse. He condemns it.

In the Bible, God stands fiercely against those who harm the vulnerable.
Jesus Himself warned that it would be better for someone to be drowned than to harm a child (Matthew 18:6).

That’s not passive language.
That’s holy anger.

So if you’ve been told, “God allowed it, so maybe it was okay…”
No.
That is not the voice of God.
So why does He allow it?
Here’s the tension we wrestle with:
God created humans with real freedom.
And real freedom means the possibility of real evil.
From the beginning, when humanity turned away from God, sin entered the world—and with it came violence, betrayal, abuse. (Genesis 3)

God could remove all evil instantly…
but that would also mean removing human freedom entirely.
And yet—

That doesn’t make the pain easier.
It just explains the battlefield.
But here’s what we often miss…
God is not distant from abuse.
He stepped into it.

Jesus was betrayed.
Mocked.
Beaten.
Stripped of dignity.
Crucified.

The Son of God didn’t watch suffering from a distance—
He entered it.
Isaiah 53 says He was “despised and rejected… a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief.”
So when you ask, “Where was God?”
He was on the cross, taking evil head-on.
Does that mean He approves suffering?
No.
It means He is working through a broken world to bring justice, healing, and ultimate restoration.

Some justice comes now.
Much of it comes later.
Because God is not only Savior—He is Judge.

No act of abuse escapes His sight.
No injustice will go unanswered.
And here’s where grace walks in…
God doesn’t just promise justice.
He offers healing.

Psalm 34:18 says,
“The Lord is close to the brokenhearted and saves those who are crushed in spirit.”
Close.

Not far.
Not indifferent.
Close.
If you’ve been abused, hear this clearly:

What happened to you was not your fault.
God did not delight in your pain.
And your story does not end in what was done to you.
Jesus specializes in restoration—taking what was meant to destroy you and rewriting it with redemption.
You may still have questions.
That’s okay.
Faith doesn’t silence pain—it brings it to the right Person.
If this stirred something in you… don’t bury it.

Talk to God honestly.
Reach out to someone safe.
Let healing begin, even if it’s slow.
And if you’re ready:
Call on Jesus.

Not just for answers—
but for healing.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
